answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with live collaborative puzzles. Each newcomer joins random strangers to solve a fresh, seasonally rotated puzzle in real time — mapping an ivory trail across a digital tundra, say — where every member must add a distinct, checkable step. Credit lands only when the group reaches a verified solution. One operator cannot sit in dozens of live sessions at once, and rotating puzzles stop scripted farms from pre-solving them. The shared signal of genuine cooperation — different minds, one real result — is far harder to fake than a lone credential.
